analyticalQuestion: How does recurrence on a regular closed Taylor-vortex streamline separate bounded signed excursion from accumulated absolute temporal variation?
supportedClaim: For the frozen smooth exact Taylor family and recurrent terminal setting, the orbit repeatedly revisits a nonconstant periodic flux phase. Absolute temporal variation and the complete payment have cubic amplitude order, while signed positive excursion has quadratic order. Consequently every sublinear power-only absolute temporal-tail estimate is false on this family; the positive-excursion successor estimate remains open.
supportedTakeaway: Closed-orbit recurrence accumulates absolute variation circuit by circuit but leaves signed excursion at the quadratic amplitude scale.
